analyst_view.overall: Early view: Ferencvaros are unbeaten in 20 games under Balazs Borbely and won 2-0 at San Siro, while Lech Poznan are 35th with one point after a 3-1 defeat at Benfica. The numbers make Lech slight favourites at home, which sits awkwardly with the current form of both sides.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. Lech scored at Benfica but conceded three, and Ferencvaros created 3.1 xG at Milan, so there should be chances at both ends; nothing points clearly away from the site's number.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners. Lech won three corners at Benfica; with home advantage they should see more of the ball, so I stay near the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. Ferencvaros will be without Bamidele Yusuf after his red card at Milan, which two reports confirmed; that does not change much on its own and the referee is not known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.4 shots. I lean slightly lower: Lech managed only six shots at Benfica, and Ferencvaros' win in Milan came from 12 shots, so neither side has been piling up attempts.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target. Lech's five on target at Benfica from six shots and Ferencvaros' efficiency in Milan point to accuracy rather than volume, so I stay with the number.
